title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — born vere & proprie sinners; Augustine and great names deny damnation for another's sin alone
pass_a_gloss: He adds that we are born from Adam as truly proper sinners drawing a truly proper sin, then cites Augustine and other great names against damnation for another's sin alone, pointing readers to Martyr, Calvin, and Chamier already quoted in earlier pages.
pass_b_english: Nor can it be denied that we are born from Adam truly and properly sinners, and from him draw a sin truly and properly so called. Add that Augustine denies, and other theologians of great name deny, that anyone is damned for another's sin. See, if you will, the words of Martyr we cited above, p. 196, from Loci Communes, Class. 2, ch. 1, §11; and also Calvin's and Chamier's words cited above, pp. 95–98.
source_text: Nec negari potest quin nascamur ex Adamo vere & proprie peccatores, ab eoque peccatum vere & proprie sic dictum trahamus. Adde quod negat Augustinus, negant theologi alii magni nominis ob alienum peccatum quenquam damnari. Vide si placet verba Martyris a nobis laudata sup. pag. 196. ex loc. Com. Class. 2. cap. 1. §. 11. Necnon verba Calvini & Chamieci laudata sup. p. 95. 96. 97. 98.

choices.choice: Born sinners + Augustine/Martyr/Calvin/Chamier vs alien damnation
